title: Architecture & Standards - API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, and ADRs
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's architecture and standards across API design, coding practices, infrastructure provisioning, model-serving conventions, observability, performance targets, and the ADR (Architecture Decision Record) process. It is intended as a single reference for engineers and architects building or modifying production systems.

Goals:
- Provide consistent, discoverable standards that reduce operational risk and improve developer velocity.
- Ensure APIs and services are predictable, versioned, and backward-compatible wherever possible.
- Maintain clear ownership, SLO-driven observability, and repeatable infra patterns using IaC.
- Capture major architecture decisions via ADRs to preserve rationale and alternatives.

1) API Standards
Purpose: Ensure API surface is easy to use, stable, and instrumented.
Key rules:
- Design style: Use RESTful patterns for synchronous endpoints; use explicit resource-oriented URLs (e.g., /v1/models/{model_id}/infer). Use JSON for payloads and prefer OpenAPI 3.1 for specification.
- Versioning: Include version in path (v1, v2). Breaking changes require a new major version and a documented migration plan.
- Idempotency: Long-running or side-effecting operations must accept an Idempotency-Key header and be idempotent within 24 hours.
- Pagination: Use cursor-based pagination with limit and cursor. Responses must include next_cursor when more results are available.
- Error model: Use standard HTTP status codes and structured error body: {"code": "string", "message": "string", "details": {}}. Maintain a central error-code registry.
- Rate limiting: Return 429 with Retry-After; include rate-limit headers X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset.
- Contracts & Schemas: All endpoints must publish OpenAPI spec in the service repo under /api/openapi.yaml and keep examples for common success/error cases.
- Security: TLS required for all traffic. All APIs must validate tokens via our central auth gateway. Sensitive fields must be redacted from logs.

API Review Checklist (PR template):
1. OpenAPI file updated and validated.
2. Backwards compatibility verified or documented (migration plan).
3. Metrics added for request count, latency histogram, and error counts.
4. Postman/contract tests added to CI.

2) Coding Standards
Scope: Applies to all service code (Go, Python, TypeScript) that runs in production.
Standards:
- Languages: Service default is Go for latency-critical runtime, Python for orchestration/eval tooling, TypeScript for frontend/backend glue.
- Formatting & linting: Enforce gofmt/golangci-lint for Go, black/flake8 for Python, and prettier/eslint for TypeScript. CI must fail on lint errors.
- Testing: Minimum coverage: 60% for backend services; critical modules (auth, billing, routing) >=80%. Unit tests for logic, integration tests for service contracts, and e2e smoke tests for deployment pipelines.
- Type Safety: Use strict typing where supported (Go generics as appropriate; mypy for Python).
- CI/CD: All PRs must pass unit tests, linters, and API contract checks before merge.
- Code review: Two approving reviewers required for production-impacting changes. One reviewer must be from the owning team and at least one cross-team reviewer for infra/SDK changes.
- Feature flags: Use feature-flag service for gradual rollout of behavioral changes. Feature flags must be documented in the feature-flag registry.
- Secrets: No secrets in repo. Use the secrets store with managed access policies.

3) Infrastructure Standards
Goal: Reproducible, auditable infra managed via IaC.
Rules:
- IaC: Terraform v1.5+ for cloud infra. All modules must be in the terraform-modules org repo and versioned. Changes to shared modules require module-level review and a migration plan.
- Environment parity: Maintain staging and prod stacks with identical Terraform modules and only config differences via variables and workspaces.
- Naming & tagging: Resources must use the naming schema: rdx-{team}-{service}-{env}-{resource}. Required tags: team, service, environment, cost_center, owner.
- Networks: VPCs must follow the reference architecture; internal services should be private subnets with NAT for egress when required. No public subnets for runtime GPUs.
- IAM & least privilege: Follow the RBAC templates. No broad wildcards in policies.
- Secrets & KMS: Use customer-managed keys for private deployments; cloud KMS for hosted. Access audits enabled and rotated annually or on key compromise.
- Capacity & quotas: Provisioning requests for Dedicated pools must follow the capacity-planning runbook and be submitted 10 business days prior to expected need.

4) Model-Serving Standards
Scope: Standards for packaging, serving, and evolving model variants in the serving runtime.
Standards:
- Packaging: Models must be packaged with metadata.json (model_id, version, architecture, tokenizer, expected_max_seq_len, quantization_profile). Artifacts stored in model registry (S3) with immutable versioned keys.
- Compatibility: Each model release must declare one or more runtime-compatible variants (fp16, int8-quantized) and the supported runtime versions.
- Warmup & caching: Provide a warmup profile (sequence of prompts) used during deployment. Runtime should support prefix and KV caching; recommended warmup tokens: 512 tokens across 4-shot prompts.
- Batching: Services should expose adaptive batching configuration with targets for tail latency. Default batch_size and max_latency_per_batch must be tunable via runtime config and documented in the model's performance profile.
- Quality & evals: Each model variant must have an associated eval set and quality baseline. Degradation beyond 3% relative to baseline triggers automatic rollback.
- Rollouts: Use canary rollouts (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated metrics checks (latency, error rate, quality signals) and explicit rollback criteria.
- Telemetry: Model-specific metrics: tokens_emitted, kv_cache_hit_rate, batch_size_distribution, quantization_fallbacks.

5) Observability Standards
Objective: Ensure fast detection and diagnosis of incidents; make systems SLO-driven.
Requirements:
- Metrics: Expose metrics as Prometheus scrape targets. Core metrics: request_count, request_latency_seconds (histogram with p50/p95/p99), error_count (4xx/5xx separate), tokens_generated, model_inference_time.
- Tracing: Instrument critical paths with OpenTelemetry. Traces must include trace ids and span ids propagated through API gateway, routing, and runtime.
- Logging: Structured JSON logs with keys: timestamp, level, service, env, request_id, user_id (when available), model_id, message. Sensitive fields must be redacted.
- Dashboards: Ownership: each service must maintain a dashboard in Grafana listing SLOs, latency heatmaps, error trends, and capacity utilization.
- Alerts: Alerting rules should be actionable and paged to oncall. Avoid high-frequency noisy alerts. Example alert triggers:
  - Error rate > 1% for 5m (pager)
  - p95 latency > target for 10m (pager)
  - SLO burn rate > 3x over 1h (pager)
  - Disk pressure or out-of-memory events on runtime hosts (pager)
- SLOs & Error Budgets: Define service-level SLOs as follows: availability 99.9% monthly (hosted control plane), inference p95 latency targets per model class (see Performance section). Error budget policy: when burn rate > 2x for 24h, initiate a severity review and halt non-essential feature rollouts.

6) Performance Standards
Purpose: Set measurable, model-class specific targets so engineering can optimize for cost and latency.
Model class performance targets (examples):
- Small models (<7B): p95 inference latency <= 150ms for single-token streaming, throughput >= 2000 tokens/s on standard CPU-optimized instances (where applicable).
- Medium models (7B-30B): p95 <= 350ms, throughput >= 600 tokens/s on GPU T4-like.
- Large models (>30B): p95 <= 700ms, throughput scaled horizontally; prefer pipeline parallel or sharded runtimes.
Notes:
- Targets are measured on realistic request mixes and must be included in the model's performance profile.
- Batching and KV caching strategies should be tuned per workload; prefer latency-aware batching for interactive endpoints.
- Quantization profiles should be approved by research and listed in quantization-profiles catalog.

7) Decision Records (ADRs)
Process:
- Every non-trivial architecture or standards decision must be recorded as an ADR. Use the ADR template in the repo: title, context, decision, alternatives considered, consequences, date, and owner.
- ADRs live in the architecture repo under /adrs and must reference related PRs, RFCs, and performance data.
- Review cadence: Monthly ADR review meeting; long-lived ADRs should be revisited at least annually or when new evidence arises.
Example recent ADRs to reference:
1. ADR-2026-01: Default model quantization strategy (decision: int8 by default for medium models with fallback to fp16).
2. ADR-2026-03: API versioning policy (decision: path-based major versioning with strict deprecation timelines).

Appendices
A. API Error Code Registry (excerpt):
- MODEL_NOT_FOUND (404): Model id not found.
- INSUFFICIENT_QUOTA (403): Customer quota exceeded.
- MODEL_DEGRADED (503): Model failing quality checks; fallback triggered.

B. SLO Table (examples):
| Component | Metric | Target | Window | Owner |
| control-plane | availability | 99.9% | monthly | platform-team |
| inference-small | p95 latency | <=150ms | 24h | serving-runtime |
| inference-medium | p95 latency | <=350ms | 24h | serving-runtime |

C. ADR template (single-line summary):
- Title: ADR-YYYY-NN - Short title
- Status: proposed | accepted | deprecated
- Context: Why the decision is needed
- Decision: The decision made and rationale
- Alternatives: Brief alternatives considered
- Consequences: Operational and technical consequences

Governance & Ownership:
- Standards steward: eng-arch team owns these standards and is responsible for updates and cross-team reviews.
- Exceptions: Requests for exceptions should be filed via the exceptions template in /policies-and-process and require approval from eng-arch and security for >30 days deviations.

How to use this document:
- Link to this page in every service README and PRs that touch API surface, infra, or model-serving components.
- Use the API Review Checklist and ADR template for new designs.
- For urgent infra changes, follow the change-management policy and notify oncall before deployment.
